{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2017}}
'''Mohammed Naseer Khan''' ({{langx|ur|محمد نصیر خان}}; 1941  – 10 July 2006) was a Pakistani [[physicist]] and [[Academic administration|academic administrator]] who served as a Rector of the [[Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology]] and later as a Vice-Chancellor of [[Bahauddin Zakariya University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://jadoons.com/notable-jadoons/|title=Notable Jadoons|date=2009-01-27|newspaper=JADOONS|language=en-US|access-date=2017-01-27}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/archive/amp/14984-country-loses-one-of-the-%E2%80%98most-productive%E2%80%99-scientists|title=Country loses one of the 'most productive' scientists|website=www.thenews.com.pk|date=3 October 2015 |language=en|access-date=2017-01-28}}</ref> He also served as a special advisor to the government for education, Federal Minister, Grade MP-1.

== Early life ==
Khan was born in 1941 in [[Abbottabad|Abbottabad, Pakistan]]. His family were local nobility and from the [[Jadun|Jadoon]] tribe;<ref name=":1" /> his father was a police officer and his mother a homemaker.

== Education and career ==
In 1996, he took a position as the [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of the Faculty of Engineering Sciences at the [[Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology|GIKI Institute]] in [[Topi, Pakistan]], and later became the university's [[Prorector]] and then [[Rector (academia)|Rector]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/360526/swabi-researchers-urged-to-help-solve-country-s-problems|title=SWABI: Researchers urged to help solve country's problems|date=2004-06-01|newspaper=DAWN.COM|language=en|access-date=2017-01-28}}</ref>{{Citation needed|date=January 2017}} He also established a research laboratory on the ‘Fabrication and Characterisation of Advanced Materials’ in the Faculty of Engineering Sciences.<ref name=":0" />

After serving as Rector of GIKI, Khan became the Vice-Chancellor of [[Bahauddin Zakariya University]] in May 2005. There "he endeavoured to create conducive work environment in the previously politicised and troubled institution and took unprecedented bold steps to achieve outstanding results."<ref name=":0" />

== Death ==
Khan was killed on [[Pakistan International Airlines Flight 688]], which crashed in [[Multan]] on 10 July 2006, killing all 45 passengers and crew aboard. A memorial service was also held in Bahrain.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archives.gdnonline.com/NewsDetails.aspx?date=04/07/2015&storyid=148944|title=Gulf Daily News » Local News » University's ex-professor killed in plane crash |website=archives.gdnonline.com|access-date=2017-01-28}}</ref>

== Awards ==
* [[Sitara-i-Imtiaz]], awarded for services to education in the field of physics, 2002<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/52557/two-foreigners-among-94-conferred-civil-awards|title=Two foreigners among 94 conferred civil awards|date=2002-08-14|newspaper=DAWN.COM|language=en|access-date=2017-01-28}}</ref>
* [[Pride of Performance]] (1998)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://beta.dawn.com/news/200868/victims-leave-a-large-number-of-mourners|title=Victims leave a large number of mourners|first=Dawn|last=Report|date=11 July 2006|website=Dawn}}</ref>
